newsitem.title: UK: UK currency strength hits profit forecasts - paper.
newsitem.headline: UK currency strength hits profit forecasts - paper.

text.p: Reductions in stockbroker forecasts for profits from two of Britain's biggest exporters have underlined fears about the impact of sterling's recent rise on British industry, the Financial Times said on Friday.

British Steel and ICI were the latest to be hit by currency worries and the latest revisions followed reductions late last year when Guinness and other drinks companies came under particular scrutiny for their exposure to sterling.

Merrill Lynch cut its forecast for British Steel for 1997-98 to 280 million pounds ($472.8 million) from 650 million pounds while HSBC James Capel trimmed its estimates on ICI for 1997 by 100 million pounds ($168.9 million) to 750 million pounds ($1.27 billion).

According to the Financial Times, broker Kleinwort Benson estimated the pound's rise would cut earnings by non-financial UK quoted companies by an average of 2.1 percent in 1996, increasing perhaps to 2.5 percent during 1997.
